pr_title: Windows: Re-create custom NAT networks after restart if missing from HNS
pr_body:
**- What I did**
Revisited on logic added by #20478 to correctly handle non-default NAT networks on Windows after server restart.
Closes #43408

**- How I did it**
Added logic which will re-create those networks with same settings after deleting orphan.

**- How to verify it**
1. Create custom network and start container to it:
```powershell
docker network create --driver nat test
docker run --net test --restart always --name test -d mcr.microsoft.com/windows/servercore:ltsc2022 ping -t 127.0.0.1
```
2. Restart server and check that test container is running.

Test binary can be found from https://filebin.net/t5nyuqjjx7un8lpd/dockerd.exe
However note that only networks which are not already missing/broken before switching to new binary version will works correctly because current behavior is that those networks get totally removed from Docker.

Windows Server 2019 does not start containers automatically on reboot, even when all docker-compose are labelled as restart: always.

<!--

**Steps to reproduce the issue:**
1. Open PowerShell with admin privileges.
2. Run any docker-compose file: `docker-compose up`
```
version: "3"

services:

  postgres_db:
    image: stellirin/postgres-windows:12-1809
    restart: always
    environment:
      - POSTGRES_USER=postgres
      - POSTGRES_PASSWORD=password
    ports:
      - "5432:5432"
```
3. Execute Restart-Computer.
When the machine starts up, execute docker ps in PowerShell with admin privileges.

Running `docker start $(docker ps -a -q -f status=exited)` returns:

comments:
I think that support for those non-default NAT networks in Windows are not ever fully implemented which why there is known bugs. Workaround is use default one by adding this to compose file:
```yaml
networks:
  default:
    external:
      name: nat
```

However as you looks to be running PostgreSQL I highly recommend to use Linux version of it instead. Linux implementation of Docker is much more well tested.

Hello ! I faced the same issue recently and I applied this same workaround, but I definitely don't understand waht is the root cause.
If you create a container and a network with the non default network it works perfectly until the machine reboot.

I traced a lot of things, and the issue seems around Hyper-V VM Swithches because it deletes and recreates network interfaces after each reboot. That cause "network xxxx not found" when the container tries to start. But if you look at `docker network ls` you see you "new" network with the same name but a different sha256.

I also tried to stick at maximum to the default network config so I tried something like :
```yaml
networks:
  elastic:
    driver: nat
    driver_opts:
      com.docker.network.windowsshim.networkname: elastic
```
To have a named network interface, but in this case, at reboot the interface s not even recreated !
Saying that, what I didn't tried is to name the interface "nat"... Maybe it could work by some magic...

Anyway, what I don't really understand is **how** it works for the default nat network !? because the behaviour seems the same (adapter deleted and recreated).

Which component is not doing its job as expected ?
* moby 
* hcsshim
* hyper-v

@gillg as far I know the issue is that libnetwork is not aware that HNS does remove those networks and it should re-create them. Default "nat" network gets created because after same way like it does after when dockerd is started first time on new server.

You can see that behavior by checking with PowerShell command `Get-HnsNetwork` before and after service reboot / server reboot.

FYI. I created now PR #43836 to fix this issue and provided test binary with fix included to there. Please, test it and provide feedback to that pull request as most of the maintainers here are only using Linux and will appreciate review help from others.

FYI: Added backport PRs to release versions as well:
* #43859
* #43858
